note: London-open read, Mon 2026-11-23 (~12:40 AM CT, Asia session). Relief bounce after Wall Street's worst week in years — S&P futures +2.2%, Nasdaq +3% — as Dec Fed hike bets eased at the margin (50bp tail now zero) and gold rebounded off the 14-month low. Dollar eased off Thursday's 19-month high — DXY 103.80 — with the yen the exception: USD/JPY 158.96 (+0.29%) as the haven bid faded on a Japan holiday. Gold $3,610 (+2.46% vs Friday's $3,523.55 close) on easing forced selling; Brent $92.55 (-0.29%) and WTI $83.31 (-0.75%) after the Sunday reopen dip. NZ retail sales smashed expectations (+2.2% q/q vs 0.5%) and Australia's flash composite PMI hit a five-year low (46.1) — both ahead of Wednesday's AU CPI and the Dec 9 RBNZ. PBoC set the yuan fix at 6.7120 vs 6.6775 estimated — a softer-yuan signal. US markets closed Thursday for Thanksgiving; Wednesday's 7:30am CT cluster (core PCE, Q3 GDP 2nd estimate, claims) is the week's big data day. Spot levels are indicative index quotes, not executable prices.
